drug_class: Nucleoside/Nucleotide Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) — Antiretroviral combination
purpose: This medicine is used to treat HIV infection in adults and children, and it is also used to help prevent HIV infection in people who are at high risk of getting it (this is called PrEP). It is always used as part of a complete HIV treatment plan and does not cure HIV, but it helps keep the virus under control.
how_it_works: HIV is a virus that attacks your immune system. This medication works by blocking a key tool the virus needs to copy itself inside your body, called reverse transcriptase. By blocking this step, the medicine helps stop HIV from multiplying and spreading, keeping your immune system stronger and healthier.
common_side_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, tiredness, and trouble sleeping are common, especially when you first start. Some people notice mild stomach upset. These side effects often improve after the first few weeks.
warnings: This medicine can affect your kidneys over time, so your doctor will check your kidney function regularly. It can also cause a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis (a dangerous build-up of acid in the blood) — tell your doctor right away if you feel very weak, have stomach pain, or have trouble breathing. If you also have hepatitis B, stopping this medicine suddenly can cause a serious flare-up of hepatitis, so never stop without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is one tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. It is very important to take it at the same time every day and not to miss doses, because skipping doses can allow the virus to become resistant to the medicine.
